question_html: How is goodwill defined from an accounting and business perspective?

options.A: The physical assets owned by a firm minus its outside liabilities
options.B: The value of reputation of a firm in respect of profits expected in future over and above the normal rate of profits
options.C: The total capital contributed by all partners initially
options.D: The accumulated reserves and surplus of the business

answer_html: Answer: (B) Goodwill is the value of reputation of a firm in respect of profits expected in future over and above the normal rate of profits[cite: 21].

question_html: Which of the following best classifies goodwill as an asset type?

options.A: Tangible Current Asset
options.B: Fictitious Asset
options.C: Intangible Asset
options.D: Liquid Asset

answer_html: Answer: (C) Goodwill is an intangible asset; it cannot be seen, felt, or transported physically, but it has monetary or saleable value[cite: 21].

question_html: In which of the following cases does the necessity for valuation of goodwill NOT arise?

options.A: When the profit-sharing ratio amongst partners is changed
options.B: When a new partner is admitted
options.C: When a routine monthly bank reconciliation statement is prepared
options.D: When the business is dissolved or sold

answer_html: Answer: (C) Valuation of goodwill arises when profit-sharing ratio changes, a partner is admitted, retires, dies, or when business is dissolved/sold, but not for routine bank reconciliations[cite: 21].

question_html: A small book business owned by a firm has net worth (assets minus liabilities) of ₹1,40,000. If a purchaser is willing to pay ₹1,50,000 for it, what does the extra ₹10,000 represent?

options.A: Accumulated profits
options.B: Goodwill
options.C: Capital reserve
options.D: Fictitious loss

answer_html: Answer: (B) The extra amount paid over and above net assets (₹1,50,000 - ₹1,40,000 = ₹10,000) is known in accounting as goodwill[cite: 21].

question_html: Which of the following factors does NOT directly affect the value of a firm's goodwill?

options.A: Favorable location of business premises
options.B: Possession of trademarks and patents
options.C: Personal political affiliations of the external auditor
options.D: Quality of goods sold and managerial skill

answer_html: Answer: (C) Factors affecting goodwill include location, trademarks, patents, quality of goods, managerial skill, etc., but not the auditor's political affiliations[cite: 21].

question_html: According to Accounting Standards, when should an enterprise recognize an intangible asset like goodwill?

options.A: Whenever management estimates self-generated brand value
options.B: Only when consideration in money or money's worth has been paid for it (purchased goodwill)
options.C: Whenever profits exceed industry averages
options.D: At the end of every financial year based on valuation

answer_html: Answer: (B) Goodwill should be recorded in books only when some consideration in money or money's worth has been paid for it (purchased goodwill)[cite: 21].

question_html: Why is internally generated (inherent) goodwill not permitted to be raised in the books of accounts?

options.A: Because it is an identifiable resource like a patent
options.B: Because its cost cannot be measured reliably in the absence of consideration paid in money or money's worth
options.C: Because future economic benefits flow to others
options.D: Because it is prohibited by the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

answer_html: Answer: (B) Internally generated goodwill cannot be recorded because its cost cannot be measured reliably without objective documentary evidence of consideration paid[cite: 21].

question_html: What should be done if a goodwill account already exists in the books of a partnership firm at the time of its reconstitution?

options.A: It should be revalued upwards
options.B: It should be written off immediately
options.C: It should be carried forward indefinitely as an asset
options.D: It should be transferred to general reserve

answer_html: Answer: (B) In case when the goodwill account exists at the time of reconstitution of firm, it should be written off immediately whether internally generated or bought for consideration[cite: 21].

question_html: How should the value of self-generated goodwill calculated during reconstitution be adjusted in the accounts?

options.A: Raised as an asset in the balance sheet
options.B: Adjusted through the capital accounts of the partners
options.C: Credited to Profit and Loss Account
options.D: Ignored entirely without any adjustment

answer_html: Answer: (B) The value of self-generated goodwill should be adjusted through the capital accounts of the partner(s) of the firm without raising a goodwill account[cite: 21].
topic_text: Adjustment of Goodwill via Capital Accounts

question_html: Which of the following is NOT one of the broad categories of methods for goodwill valuation?

options.A: Average profit basis
options.B: Super profit basis
options.C: Liquidation basis
options.D: Capitalization basis

answer_html: Answer: (C) The three methods for goodwill valuation are Average profit basis, Super profit basis, and Capitalization basis[cite: 21].

question_html: When should the weighted average profit method be preferred over the simple average profit method for valuing goodwill?

options.A: When profits fluctuate randomly without any pattern
options.B: When there exists a clear increasing or decreasing trend of profits
options.C: When the firm suffers continuous net losses
options.D: When capital employed is zero

answer_html: Answer: (B) Weighted average is used when profit has an increasing or decreasing trend, giving highest weight to the current year[cite: 21].

question_html: How is Normal Profit calculated under the super profit method?

options.A: Average Profit minus Actual Profit
options.B: Normal Rate of Return (NRR) multiplied by Capital Employed
options.C: Total past profits divided by number of years
options.D: Capital employed multiplied by years of purchase

answer_html: Answer: (B) Normal Profit = Normal Rate of Return (NRR) $ imes$ Capital Employed[cite: 21].

question_html: What does Super Profit represent in business valuation?

options.A: Total revenue earned by the firm
options.B: Excess profit that can be earned by a firm over and above the normal profit usually earned by similar firms
options.C: Profit earned before charging partners' salaries
options.D: Capital contributions made by incoming partners

answer_html: Answer: (B) Super profit means excess profit that can be earned by a firm over and above the normal profit usually earned by similar firms under similar circumstances[cite: 21].

question_html: What is the main drawback of the 'number of years purchase of super profit' method?

options.A: It ignores historical cost
options.B: Time value of money is not considered
options.C: It requires complex actuarial tables
options.D: It assumes zero capital employed

answer_html: Answer: (B) The major drawback of the number of years purchase method is that the time value of money is not considered[cite: 21].
topic_text: Drawback of Number of Years Purchase

question_html: How is goodwill calculated under the Capitalization of Average Profit method?

options.A: Super Profit divided by Normal Rate of Return
options.B: Capitalized value of business (Average Profit / NRR) minus Actual Capital Employed (Net Tangible Assets)
options.C: Average Profit multiplied by number of years purchase
options.D: Capital Employed multiplied by NRR

answer_html: Answer: (B) Goodwill = Value of the firm (Capitalized average profit) minus Net Assets (Capital Employed)[cite: 21].

question_html: What is 'Hidden' or 'Implied' goodwill?

options.A: Goodwill recorded in secret books of accounts
options.B: Goodwill that is not specifically given and has to be inferred from the arrangement of capital or profit-sharing ratio when a new partner is admitted
options.C: Goodwill arising from illegal business activities
options.D: Goodwill bought in cash and immediately withdrawn

answer_html: Answer: (B) Sometimes the value of goodwill is not specifically given and has to be inferred or implied from the arrangement of capital or profit-sharing ratio[cite: 21].

question_html: In case of admission of a new partner, premium for goodwill brought in by the new partner is credited to existing partners in which ratio?

options.A: New profit-sharing ratio
options.B: Old profit-sharing ratio
options.C: Profit sacrificing ratio
options.D: Capital contribution ratio

answer_html: Answer: (C) The premium for goodwill brought in by the new partner shall be given to existing partners who have sacrificed a part of their profits, based on profit sacrificing ratio[cite: 21].

question_html: What entry is passed in the books of the firm when an incoming partner pays premium for goodwill privately to existing partners?

options.A: Debit Cash A/c and Credit Goodwill A/c
options.B: Debit New Partner's Capital A/c and Credit Old Partners' Capital A/c
options.C: No entry is required in the books of the firm
options.D: Debit Premium for Goodwill A/c and Credit Bank A/c

answer_html: Answer: (C) When the incoming partner pays any premium for goodwill privately to the existing partners, no entry is required in the books of the firm[cite: 21].

question_html: In case of retirement or death of a partner, how is their share of goodwill adjusted among continuing partners?

options.A: Credited to retiring partner and debited to continuing partners in their gaining ratio
options.B: Debited to retiring partner and credited to continuing partners in sacrificing ratio
options.C: Written off against general reserve equally
options.D: Ignored because goodwill cannot be valued upon retirement

answer_html: Answer: (A) Continuing partners gain in profit-sharing ratio upon retirement/death, so they compensate the retiring/deceased partner's share of goodwill in the gaining ratio[cite: 21].

question_html: How is profit sacrificing ratio computed?

options.A: New Profit Sharing Ratio minus Old Profit Sharing Ratio
options.B: Old Profit Sharing Ratio minus New Profit Sharing Ratio
options.C: Capital Contribution Ratio divided by 2
options.D: Gaining Ratio plus New Ratio

answer_html: Answer: (B) The profit sacrificing ratio is computed by deducting the new profit sharing ratio from the old profit sharing ratio[cite: 21].

question_html: The past profits of five years of a partnership firm are: ₹50,000; ₹40,000; ₹52,000; ₹48,000 and ₹56,000 respectively. What is the value of goodwill on the basis of 4 years' purchase of the average profits of the last five years?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total profits = ₹2,46,000; Average profit = ₹49,200; Goodwill = 4 $ imes$ ₹49,200 = ₹1,96,800[cite: 21].

question_html: A partnership firm earned profits for four years: ₹70,000; ₹80,000; ₹1,20,000 and ₹1,00,000. Total capital investment is ₹4,50,000. Reasonable expected return is 15%. What is the value of goodwill based on 3 years' purchase of average super profits?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Average profit = ₹92,500; Normal profit = 15% of ₹4,50,000 = ₹67,500; Super profit = ₹25,000; Goodwill = ₹25,000 $ imes$ 3 = ₹75,000[cite: 21].

question_html: Annual maintainable profit after tax is ₹65,000. Capital employed is ₹4,00,000. Normal rate of return is 12% p.a. If the present value of an annuity of ₹1 for five years at 12% is 3.604776, what is the value of goodwill under the annuity method?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Super profit = ₹65,000 - (12% of ₹4,00,000) = ₹17,000; Goodwill under annuity method = ₹17,000 $ imes$ 3.604776 = ₹61,281 (approx)[cite: 21].

question_html: Net tangible assets of a firm are worth ₹4,10,000 and average profit of the last four years is ₹60,000. What is the value of goodwill under capitalization method if reasonable return is 12%?

M/s Lee and Lawson earned profits: 2019: ₹1,20,000; 2020: ₹1,25,000; 2021: ₹1,30,000; 2022: ₹1,50,000. Capital employed on 31.12.2022 was ₹5,00,000 and normal rate of profit is 20%. Using weighted average profit (weights 1, 2, 3, 4) and 3 years purchase of super profit, what is the value of goodwill?

Capital invested is ₹1,50,000. Trading results: 2019: Profit ₹40,000; 2020: Profit ₹36,000; 2021: Loss ₹6,000; 2022: Profit ₹50,000. Market interest rate is 10%, risk return is 2%, proprietor's alternative remuneration is ₹6,000 p.a. What is the super profit based on average of last 4 years?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total profit = ₹1,20,000; Average profit = ₹30,000; Less remuneration ₹6,000 = Maintainable profit ₹24,000; Normal profit = 12% of ₹1,50,000 = ₹18,000; Super profit = ₹24,000 - ₹18,000 = ₹6,000[cite: 21].

question_html: A's capital is ₹20,000 and B's capital is ₹15,000 sharing profits equally. C is admitted with ₹18,000 capital for 1/4th share. What is the hidden/inferred goodwill of the firm?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total capital ought to be ₹18,000 $ imes$ 4 = ₹72,000. Actual combined capital of A, B, and C = ₹20,000 + ₹15,000 + ₹18,000 = ₹53,000. Hidden goodwill = ₹72,000 - ₹53,000 = ₹19,000[cite: 21].

question_html: Yellow and Green share profits 3:2. Balance sheet shows capital: Yellow ₹25,000, Green ₹20,000. Black is admitted for 5/16th share with ₹20,000 capital. Goodwill is valued at ₹36,000. What is Black's share of goodwill to be adjusted?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Black's share of goodwill = (₹36,000 / 16) $ imes$ 5 = ₹11,250[cite: 21].

question_html: A, B & C are equal partners. They want to change their profit sharing ratio to 4:3:2. Goodwill of the firm is valued at ₹90,000. What is the amount of compensation paid by A to C?
answer_html: Answer: (A) A's gain = 4/9 - 1/3 = 1/9; C's loss = 1/3 - 2/9 = 1/9; Compensation = ₹90,000 $ imes$ (1/9) = ₹10,000[cite: 21].

question_html: Antoo, Bantoo and Chintoo share profits 3:4:3. Goodwill is valued at ₹3,60,000. Antoo retires. Bantoo and Chintoo share future profits equally. What is Antoo's share of goodwill debited to Bantoo and Chintoo in their gaining ratio?

options.A: Bantoo ₹36,000, Chintoo ₹72,000
options.B: Bantoo ₹54,000, Chintoo ₹54,000
options.C: Bantoo ₹72,000, Chintoo ₹36,000
options.D: Bantoo ₹40,000, Chintoo ₹68,000

answer_html: Answer: (A) Antoo's share = 3/10 of ₹3,60,000 = ₹1,08,000. Gaining ratio of Bantoo and Chintoo is 1:2. Bantoo bears ₹36,000 and Chintoo bears ₹72,000[cite: 21].

question_html: What does the term 'Annuity' mean in the context of goodwill valuation by the annuity method?

options.A: Variable annual bonus paid to retiring partners
options.B: Identical annual amount of super profit discounted to present value
options.C: Total accumulated reserves over the life of the firm
options.D: Annual depreciation charged on fixed assets

answer_html: Answer: (B) The word annuity is used to mean identical annual amount of super profit, which is discounted using an annuity table[cite: 21].

question_html: Why must partners who gain in profit-sharing ratio compensate partners who sacrifice during firm reconstitution?

options.A: Because the Partnership Act mandates a fixed transfer fee
options.B: Because the gaining partners acquire a larger share of future profits generated by the firm's overall reputation and efforts
options.C: To clear outstanding tax liabilities of the firm
options.D: To pay commission to external auditors

answer_html: Answer: (B) Those sacrificing future profit should be compensated by others who gain, as the gaining partners secure a greater share of future profits[cite: 21].

question_html: Which condition is NOT required for recognizing an intangible asset under Accounting Standards?

options.A: Must have characteristics of an asset and be clearly identifiable
options.B: Future probable economic benefits must flow to the enterprise
options.C: Cost of the intangible asset must be measurable reliably
options.D: Must be generated internally through long-term advertising without monetary exchange

answer_html: Answer: (D) Internally generated goodwill without monetary consideration cannot be recognized; AS requirements specify identifiable resource, probable economic benefits, and reliably measurable cost[cite: 21].
topic_text: AS Recognition Criteria for Intangible Assets

question_html: When weighting past profits, which year is assigned the highest weight?

options.A: The earliest past year
options.B: The current / most recent year
options.C: The median year
options.D: All years receive equal weights

answer_html: Answer: (B) Highest weight is always given to the current year, as it reflects a more realistic view of future profitability[cite: 21].

question_html: What does 'Capital Employed' typically signify in partnership accounts for goodwill valuation?

options.A: Total gross revenue minus total expenses
options.B: Net tangible assets (Assets minus outside liabilities) invested in the business
options.C: Only the cash balance at bank
options.D: Total loan borrowed from partners

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital employed represents net tangible assets invested in the business, calculated as assets minus liabilities[cite: 21].

question_html: Wise, Clever and Dull share profits 4:3:3. On June 30, 2022, Wise died. Goodwill is valued at 3 years' purchase of average profits of past 3 years after deducting 8% interest on capital employed (₹1,56,000) and fair remuneration (₹15,000 p.a. per partner). Profits: 2019: ₹67,200; 2020: ₹75,600; 2021: ₹72,000; 2022: ₹62,400 (assumed earned evenly). What is the 3-year average profit ending 30th June 2022?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Average profit for 3 years ending 30th June 2022 calculated across prorated periods equals ₹70,800[cite: 21].
topic_text: Death of Partner Average Profit Calculation

question_html: In question 36, average future maintainable profit after deducting total partner remuneration (₹45,000) and 8% interest on capital employed (₹12,480) from ₹70,800 is:
Based on question 37, what is Wise's share of goodwill (4/10th) if firm goodwill is 3 years' purchase of ₹13,320?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Firm goodwill = ₹13,320 $ imes$ 3 = ₹39,960; Wise's share = 4/10 of ₹39,960 = ₹15,984[cite: 21].

question_html: Cu and Au share profits 5:3. On April 1, 2022, Ag is admitted for 1/4th share with ₹2,00,000 capital. New ratio is 2:1:1. Adjusted weighted average profit is ₹1,80,000. Goodwill is 3 years' purchase. What is Ag's share of goodwill in cash?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Firm goodwill = ₹1,80,000 $ imes$ 3 = ₹5,40,000; Ag's share (1/4th) = ₹1,35,000[cite: 21].

question_html: A, B & C are equal partners. They wanted to take D who brought in ₹36,000 as goodwill. New profit sharing ratio is 3:3:2:2. What is the sacrifice ratio of A, B and C?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Sacrificing ratio: A = 1/3 - 3/10 = 1/30; B = 1/3 - 3/10 = 1/30; C = 1/3 - 2/10 = 4/30; ratio is 1:1:4[cite: 21].

question_html: What is the primary purpose of calculating sacrificing ratio on admission of a partner?

options.A: To divide accumulated tax liabilities equally
options.B: To distribute goodwill premium brought in by the incoming partner among existing partners in proportion to their sacrifice
options.C: To determine how trade payables are settled
options.D: To calculate depreciation on fixed assets

answer_html: Answer: (B) Sacrificing ratio is used to distribute goodwill premium brought in by the incoming partner among existing partners who sacrificed profit share[cite: 21].

question_html: If a new partner's profit-sharing share is given without specifying details of how old partners sacrifice, what is assumed regarding the old partners' sacrificing ratio?

options.A: It is equal to their new profit sharing ratio
options.B: It is equal to their old profit sharing ratio
options.C: It is always in the ratio of capital contributions
options.D: All sacrifice is borne by the senior-most partner alone

answer_html: Answer: (B) If only the new partner's profit sharing is given, the profit sacrificing ratio of old partners would be the same as their old profit sharing ratio[cite: 21].

question_html: What entry is passed when goodwill brought in cash by a new partner is withdrawn by old partners?

options.A: Debit Old Partners' Capital Accounts and Credit Bank Account
options.B: Debit Bank Account and Credit Old Partners' Capital Accounts
options.C: Debit Goodwill Account and Credit Cash Account
options.D: No entry is passed

answer_html: Answer: (A) When goodwill brought in cash is withdrawn, old partners' capital accounts are debited and bank account is credited[cite: 21].

question_html: In case of a change in profit sharing ratio among existing partners, how is goodwill treated?

options.A: It is capitalized and shown as a new asset
options.B: It is determined and preferably adjusted through capital accounts of partners on the basis of sacrificing/gaining ratio
options.C: It is written off against trade payables
options.D: It is distributed equally regardless of sacrifice

answer_html: Answer: (B) In case of change in profit sharing ratio, goodwill should be determined and preferably adjusted through capital accounts on the basis of profit sacrificing ratio[cite: 21].

question_html: What is the main characteristic that distinguishes 'purchased goodwill' from 'inherent (self-generated) goodwill'?

options.A: Purchased goodwill is recorded in books because consideration in money/money's worth was paid; inherent goodwill is not recorded
options.B: Inherent goodwill has higher depreciation rates than purchased goodwill
options.C: Purchased goodwill can only be held by corporations, not partnerships
options.D: Inherent goodwill appears in the balance sheet as a current asset

answer_html: Answer: (A) Purchased goodwill involves payment in money or money's worth and can be validly recorded, whereas self-generated goodwill cannot be recorded[cite: 21].

question_html: A, B and C are partners sharing profits in 3:2:1 ratio. They change ratio to 2:2:1 and value goodwill at ₹30,000 (not appearing in old balance sheet, nor to appear in new). What is the journal entry adjustment?

options.A: B's Capital A/c Dr. ₹2,000, C's Capital A/c Dr. ₹1,000 To A's Capital A/c ₹3,000
options.B: A's Capital A/c Dr. ₹3,000 To B's Capital A/c ₹2,000, To C's Capital A/c ₹1,000
options.C: Goodwill A/c Dr. ₹30,000 To A, B, C Capital A/cs
options.D: No entry required

answer_html: Answer: (A) A sacrificed 3/6 - 2/5 = 3/30; B gained 2/6 - 2/5 = -2/30; C gained 1/6 - 1/5 = -1/30. B and C compensate A (B: ₹30,000 $ imes$ 2/30 = ₹2,000; C: ₹30,000 $ imes$ 1/30 = ₹1,000)[cite: 21].

question_html: Profits/losses for 4 years: 2018-19: Loss ₹10,000; 2019-20: Loss ₹2,500; 2020-21: Profit ₹98,000; 2021-22: Profit ₹76,000. Average capital employed is ₹2,00,000. Interest rate on capital is 12%. Partner remuneration is estimated at ₹1,000 per month (not yet charged). What is the goodwill value based on two years' purchase of super profits?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total profit = (-10,000) + (-2,500) + 98,000 + 76,000 = ₹1,61,500; Average profit = ₹40,375; Less remuneration (₹12,000) = Maintainable profit ₹28,375; Normal profit = 12% of ₹2,00,000 = ₹24,000; Super profit = ₹4,375; Goodwill = ₹4,375 $ imes$ 2 = ₹8,750[cite: 21].
topic_text: Super Profit with Past Losses Problem

question_html: A and B share profits 5:3. C brings ₹70,000 cash and ₹48,000 against goodwill. New ratio is 7:5:4. What is the sacrificing ratio of A and B?
answer_html: Answer: (A) A's sacrifice = 5/8 - 7/16 = 3/16; B's sacrifice = 3/8 - 5/16 = 1/16; ratio is 3:1[cite: 21].

question_html: What is the difference in treatment when goodwill is brought in cash by a new partner and retained in business versus when it is withdrawn?

options.A: Retaining keeps cash in business and credits old partners; withdrawal removes cash from business via bank credit
options.B: Retaining requires a goodwill asset account to be raised
options.C: Withdrawal cancels the new partner's capital contribution
options.D: There is no accounting difference

answer_html: Answer: (A) Retaining goodwill leaves cash in the firm's bank balance while crediting old partners; withdrawal reduces bank balance as partners take the cash out[cite: 21].

question_html: Why does AS 26 restrict the recognition of internally generated goodwill?

options.A: To prevent subjective and non-verifiable asset inflation on balance sheets since cost cannot be measured reliably
options.B: Because partnerships are illegal entities
options.C: To ensure all profits are taxed at higher rates
options.D: Because intangible assets never generate cash flows

answer_html: Answer: (A) AS restricts internal goodwill recognition because cost cannot be measured reliably and lacks objective documentary evidence, preventing arbitrary inflation[cite: 21].
